subject: Edge anchor: NAT/Egress, nodeclass diversity & local-cache fallback
messages:
From: Simon Hart <simon.hart@acmeops.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Edge anchor: NAT/Egress, nodeclass diversity & local-cache fallback

Hi Vanessa / Marissa,

Thanks again for taking a look at our private cluster plan for the new SEA-42 edge anchor. We wanted to surface a couple of constraints ahead of the preflight:

- Network: site only has a single transit NAT IP block (e.g., 54.23.11.0/28) that will be used for egress. We need recommendations for NAT pooling and per-tenant SNAT to avoid port exhaustion.
- Node classes: hardware mix includes: 2x r5-like control VMs, 6x compute GPU nodes (A100-ish), and 8x mixed-storage nodes with local NVMe + 8TB rotational. We expect low-latency KV caching on local NVMe for embeddings.
- Storage: customer wants ephemeral KV cache on local NVMe, but long-term artifacts should go to an S3-target over the private link. Need clear fallback behavior if NVMe fails (hot-warm fallback, throttling).

I've attached a site inventory CSV and a rough network diagram. Can we confirm a short design call next week? Prefer Tue 8/31 10:00 PST.

Attachments: [attachment: site-inventory-20260827.csv], [attachment: egress-nat-diagram-v1.pdf]

Thanks,
Simon

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Edge anchor: NAT/Egress, nodeclass diversity & local-cache fallback

Simon — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments; landed OK. Quick replies inline and then a proposed agenda: 

- NAT/egress: we typically recommend a dual-NAT approach for single-IP sites: an application-facing SNAT pool with port-preserving behavior + a second ephemeral pool for control-plane egress (metrics, checks). We'll sketch port utilization estimates in the call.
- Nodeclass & local NVMe: we can map your mixed-storage nodes as "localcache" nodeclass with a pod-affinity profile for eviction (cold-start fallback to S3). We'll propose a short-circuit KV eviction policy and a health-check that flips read-through to S3 when disk IOPS degrade.
- Fallback plan: model will be: NVMe healthy -> read from local cache; NVMe degraded -> route reads to warm nodeclass (replica on mixed-storage) then to S3; writes always mirror to S3. This preserves correctness while minimizing latency.

Proposed call agenda (30min):
1) Confirm port requirements and NAT sizing (10m)
2) Nodeclass mapping and pod scheduling constraints (10m)
3) Failure modes and rollback (5m)
4) Next steps / runbook ownership (5m)

If that works, I'll bring a draft runbook (nodeclass and localcache failover) and loop Karthik for kernel/IO knobs. Tue 2026-08-31 10:00 PST works for us — sending a calendar invite.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Edge anchor: NAT/Egress, nodeclass diversity & local-cache fallback

Vanessa / Marissa — adding a few concrete pieces we should include in the runbook and the acceptance criteria. Quoting Simon's note below for context: 

> Network: site only has a single transit NAT IP block (e.g., 54.23.11.0/28) that will be used for egress. We need recommendations for NAT pooling and per-tenant SNAT to avoid port exhaustion.

Runbook / acceptance items (draft):
- NAT sizing: assume worst-case 16k ephemeral ports per IP; recommend we reserve 60% for app SNAT and 40% for control-plane (health checks, metrics). Provide sample iptables/NAT rules and test harness.
- Egress path policy: mark-control-plane traffic using DSCP/metadata and route via dedicated SNAT mapping to minimize contention. Document flow logs to correlate port usage per tenant.
- Nodeclass labels: 
  - node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass=localcache (local NVMe + eviction policy enabled)
  - node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass=compute-gpu (A100-tier)
  - node.k8s.redwood/nodeclass=archive (rotational-backed long term)
- Local cache fallback behavior:
  - Health probe: iostat + SMART + fio-lite check every 60s. If IOPS < threshold OR SMART errors detected -> mark node as degraded and taint: localcache=degraded:NoSchedule.
  - Pod-level controller will move affected cache pods to available warm replicas in archive/compute-gpu nodeclass (with affinity tolerations).
  - Writes are mirrored: local ephemeral write accepted, then async mirror to S3 with bounded retry (max 5 attempts) before surfacing error to app.
- Tests: simulate 1) NVMe throttling 50% IO 2) full NVMe failure 3) NAT port exhaustion. Each test has clear pass/fail.

I've put a short skeleton file in the Drive (runbook-nodeclass-draft.md) and attached it here for review. I'll bring kernel-level knobs (nr_requests, scheduler hints) to the call if we need low-level IO tuning.

Attachments: [attachment: runbook-nodeclass-draft.md]

—Kar
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
